# lookout triage status

Write (or read back) the §9.4 triage-status record for an incident — diagnosis, action taken, and your severity judgment — so health scans stop reporting it as a fresh unknown and the sentinel stops re-paging followups; the incident playbooks' closing move.

MCP tool: `k8s_triage_status`

## Usage

    lookout triage status [flags]

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--store` | — | path to the sentinel's SQLite store (its --store file). Required: triage-status records live in the sentinel's --store SQLite file (§9.4); see docs/triage-status-write-design.md |
| `--fingerprint` | — | the incident-class fingerprint from the inject payload or store row (§8, sha256:…). Required to write; to read, this or --resource selects the record(s) |
| `--resource` | — | resource key pinning the record to one object: <KindOfObject>/<namespace>/<name> (namespace segment empty for cluster-scoped objects, e.g. Node//gke-node-1). Required to write |
| `--status` | — | triage state to record: investigating\|triaged\|actioned\|escalated (resolved is written by the sentinel's §7.4 recovery flip, never by agents). Empty = read mode: print the current record(s) instead of writing |
| `--session` | — | incident session id that produced this record — the paper trail's pointer back to the transcript |
| `--root-cause` | — | root-cause hypothesis one-liner |
| `--severity-override` | — | your routing judgment for further signals of this incident: critical\|warning\|info (empty = keep the signal's own class). Honored by sentinel routing and health scans while the record is open |
| `--action` | — | action taken / paper trail ("fix PR opened; config rollout pending") |

## Common flags (every lookout command)

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` | — | limit the scan to one namespace |
| `-A` | — | scan all namespaces |
| `--workload` | — | target one workload as <Kind>/<namespace>/<name>, e.g. Deployment/prod/api |
| `--since` | — | how far back to look (0 = command default) |
| `--format` | logfmt | output format: logfmt\|json (one record per line either way) |
| `--timeout` | 10s | abort the invocation after this long (exit 1) |
| `--kubeconfig` | — | path to a kubeconfig file, instead of $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config |
| `--context` | — | kubeconfig context to read, instead of its current-context. Selects a cluster for THIS invocation only — nothing is written back — so concurrent invocations can target different clusters. Reported as context=<name> in the summary line |
| `--exemptions` | — | path to a git-reviewed exemption file (YAML); covered findings are ANNOTATED with their reason and expiry and counted as exempt=<n> in the summary, never dropped |

## Finding kinds

Every `kind=` this command can emit, and the severities it carries them at. Nothing else appears in its output; a kind absent from a run means the check looked and found nothing.

| Kind | Severity | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `triage.status` | info | the triage record for an incident subject as it now stands — state, root-cause hypothesis, action, and who wrote it; a receipt, not a defect |

## Output fields

Beyond the shared envelope fields (`kind`, `severity`, `namespace`, `kind_of_object`, `name`, `reason`, `message`, `fingerprint`, `exempt_reason`, `exempt_expires`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resource_key` | the record's resource pin, as stored (<KindOfObject>/<namespace>/<name>) |
| `triage_status` | the record's triage state (investigating\|triaged\|actioned\|escalated\|resolved) |
| `triage_root_cause` | the recorded root-cause hypothesis |
| `triage_action` | the recorded action / paper trail |
| `triage_session` | the incident session that wrote the record |
| `severity_override` | the recorded severity judgment (critical\|warning\|info), when one is set |
| `updated` | when the record last changed, RFC 3339 |

## Output contract

Output: one finding per line (logfmt; --format=json for one JSON object
per line), keys in fixed order; healthy resources emit nothing. The final
line is always the summary: scanned=<n> findings=<n> elapsed=<d> —
findings=0 with a summary present means "scanned and healthy"; a stream
without a summary line is void. Exit 0 data, 1 runtime error (diagnostics
on stderr only), 2 usage.

## Examples

```lookout
lookout triage status --store=/var/lib/lookout/lookout.db --fingerprint=sha256:e2957792a0b3 --resource=Pod/prod/checkout-697567895d-2gglt --session=sess-0004 --status=triaged --severity-override=warning --root-cause="DB connection string invalid in checkout-config" --action="fix PR opened; config rollout pending"
lookout triage status --store=/var/lib/lookout/lookout.db --fingerprint=sha256:e2957792a0b3
lookout triage status --store=/var/lib/lookout/lookout.db --resource=Pod/prod/checkout-697567895d-2gglt
```
